service.name: Corporate holiday party entertainment
service.serviceType: Live bands and DJs for corporate holiday parties
service.description: Live music and DJs for corporate holiday parties in Denver and along the Front Range, November and December 2026, sized to the venue and the program.

faqs.q: Which dates does the Denver holiday season cover?
faqs.a: 21 party dates across November and December 2026, 10 of them in December, covering Thursdays, Fridays and Saturdays plus New Year's Eve. The peak December dates are marked, because this market prices a holiday weekend above a standard date. Whether a date is free is a booking-calendar question: send the date and the venue.

faqs.q: When do companies book holiday party entertainment?
faqs.a: August through October is when the season is decided for November and December dates, and New Year's Eve books first of all. Booking early buys the date rather than a lower number, which on a December Saturday is the thing actually worth having.

faqs.q: What does a holiday party band cost?
faqs.a: A cover or jazz band for a corporate event runs {{market:us_corporate_band}} in this market, and a Denver holiday weekend carries {{market:denver_holiday_surcharge}} on top of a standard date. Signet does not publish prices: send the date and the venue and you get our number for that night. Travel beyond the metro is its own line.

faqs.q: Can one booking cover dinner and dancing?
faqs.a: Yes: a duo through drinks and dinner, then a DJ carrying the back half, on one contract. Once we are in the building the evening is already committed, so covering both halves that way is cheaper than hiring twice.

faqs.q: Can our procurement process clear a booking in time?
faqs.a: Yes, if it starts in October rather than December. We can be set up as a vendor, quote against a purchase order and take net-30 on approval, with a certificate of insurance naming your venue, a W-9 and one itemised invoice in the same email as the contract. Vendor onboarding is the slowest step of a corporate booking.
